page: Amazon Web Services c8i.24xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via dedicated CPU allocation with two threads per core. The processor features 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration includes a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled GPUs, and no local instance storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput across intensive workloads. The instance achieved top-tier ratings in PassMark CPU score (106,933.38), extended instructions test (135,297.39), and Geekbench multi-core execution (22,352.0). Support for AVX-512 and AMX (tile and int8) accelerators aids matrix computation and cryptographic operations. Uncached read memory bandwidth peaked at 388.68 GB/sec, supporting fast throughput for Redis SET operations at 171.2 million ops/sec and static web serving throughput of 154.92 GB/sec. LLM prompt processing reached 320.04 tokens/sec on 7B models and 41.44 tokens/sec on 70B models.

Because the server lacks local disk storage, workloads rely exclusively on remote block storage, which necessitates network-attached volumes for persistent data. The 2:1 vCPU-to-RAM profile delivers high compute efficiency per gigabyte of memory, maximizing compute density for CPU-bound tasks. Amazon Web Services c8i.24xlarge is well fitted for distributed compilation, software build pipelines, batch processing, static web fleets, Redis in-memory caching layers, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It features 48 physical cores, 96 vCPUs, and 192.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. Network connectivity provides a 40 Gbps baseline, while local storage and hardware GPU acceleration are not included. The processor supports advanced extensions including AVX-512, AMX, and AES instructions, driving top-tier benchmark scores in Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU tests, and memory read bandwidth. With strong parallel throughput, high memory bandwidth, and high-volume Redis operations, the instance offers cost-efficient compute density without paying for unused RAM overhead. It is best suited for large-scale software compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, static web serving fleets, and high-concurrency batch processing.
